question: How long does the post-natal period (puerperium) typically last in clinical practice?
explanation: You'll see this time and again in midwifery! The post-natal period is officially defined as the first six weeks after childbirth when the mother's body returns to its pre-pregnant state. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h1)

question: Why is post-natal care just as crucial as the care a mother gets during pregnancy?

options.A: Many serious health complications happen during the weeks after delivery.
options.B: The baby no longer needs any medical attention after birth.
options.C: Hormones return to normal instantly without any professional help.
options.D: It gives the mother time to rest away from her family members.

explanation: Spotting issues early saves lives! A large percentage of maternal and newborn complications happen right after birth, which is why close monitoring during the post-natal phase is a total lifesaver. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h1)

question: For a mother who had a safe, normal delivery, when should her very first post-natal check happen?

options.D: At the end of the second week

explanation: That first check within 24 hours is super important to catch immediate issues like heavy bleeding or shock before they become emergencies. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h2)

question: When is the final routine post-natal visit usually scheduled to ensure the reproductive organs have fully recovered?
explanation: The 4 to 6-week mark wraps up the puerperium! It's the perfect time for you to confirm the womb has gone back to normal size and chat about family planning. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h2)

question: What do we call the normal vaginal discharge that a mother passes as her uterus heals after birth?
explanation: Lochia is just the body's natural way of cleaning out the uterus after delivery—shedding old tissue and blood as healing takes place. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h3)

question: What color should a healthy mother's lochia look like during the first three days after delivery?
explanation: In the beginning, lochia is called 'rubra' (red) because it's mostly fresh blood and tissue. Completely normal for the first few days! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h3)

question: When you gently feel (palpate) a mother's tummy to check her uterus after birth, what is your main goal?

options.A: To confirm that the uterus is firm and contracting
options.B: To check if the bladder is completely empty
options.C: To stimulate milk production in the breasts
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the mother

explanation: A nice, hard, contracted uterus (like a firm mango!) stops bleeding. If it feels soft or boggy, that's a red flag for postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h4)

question: On day four, a new mother complains that her right calf is suddenly painful, swollen, and warm to the touch. What should pop into your head first?
explanation: Pain and swelling in just one leg after childbirth is a classic warning sign of a blood clot (DVT). Always take this seriously and report it immediately! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h4)

question: At what exact times after birth is a newborn's Apgar score routinely checked?
explanation: Think '1 and 5'! The 1-minute score shows how the baby handled the stress of birth, while the 5-minute score shows how well they are adapting to life outside the womb. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h5)

question: Why do midwives give a routine injection of Vitamin K to newborns shortly after delivery?

options.B: To build strong bones and teeth

explanation: Babies are born with very low levels of Vitamin K and sterile tummies, which puts them at risk of bleeding until their gut flora kicks in. The injection protects them safely! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h5)

question: What is the leading cause of heavy bleeding right after childbirth (early postpartum hemorrhage)?
explanation: Uterine atony simply means the womb muscle is too tired to clamp down tightly after delivery. Keeping it firm is a key part of your nursing care! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h6)

question: What is the safest way for a new mother to clean her perineal area after using the toilet?
explanation: Front to back always! This golden rule keeps germs from the anal area away from the vagina and urethra, protecting her from nasty infections. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h7)

question: Why must breastfeeding mothers make sure they drink plenty of extra fluids every day?

options.A: To replace fluids lost through breastmilk production
options.B: To flush out the kidneys and stop weight gain
options.C: To help the lochia turn white faster
options.D: To prevent the uterus from contracting too fast

explanation: Breastmilk is mostly water! If mom doesn't drink enough, her milk supply can drop and she can easily become dehydrated. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h7)

question: Which family planning pill is best for mothers who are breastfeeding in the early months because it won't dry up their milk?
explanation: Progestin-only pills (the 'minipill') are safe for nursing moms because they don't mess with breastmilk production like estrogen can. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h8)

question: What is the main health benefit of encouraging child spacing through family planning after having a baby?

options.A: It gives the mother's body time to recover its nutrient stores and strength.
options.B: It makes uterine involution happen within twenty-four hours.
options.C: It guarantees that the next baby will be a male child.
options.D: It completely stops all postpartum mood changes.

explanation: Pregnancy takes a lot out of a woman's body! Spacing pregnancies gives her time to rebuild her iron and nutrient levels so she stays strong for herself and her family. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h8)

question: What is one of the main responsibilities of community health workers when it comes to post-natal care?

options.A: Performing major surgical repairs for tears
options.B: Delivering babies in primary operating theatres
options.C: Conducting home visits and tracking immunizations
options.D: Prescribing strong antibiotics for severe sepsis

explanation: Community health workers are fantastic bridges to the community. They visit homes to make sure babies get their vaccines and moms are recovering nicely. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h9)

question: Why are home visits by community health workers so helpful for new mothers?

options.A: It replaces the need for any professional hospital assessment.
options.B: It prevents the mother from experiencing any fatigue.
options.C: It ensures the baby starts walking much earlier.
options.D: It reaches mothers who might not return to the clinic for check-ups.

explanation: Not every mother can make it back to the clinic due to distance or traditions. Community outreach ensures these mothers aren't left stranded with hidden health issues. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h9)
